summary: No Maluku-specific ordinance, police operation, court ruling, protection scheme or trans-specific incident appears in the sources reviewed for this province, so no Maluku-specific finding is available and the national assessment for Indonesia applies here unchanged.
tangentialFactors: No Maluku measure criminalising same-sex conduct is recorded; the sub-national criminalisation documented for Indonesia is confined to provinces elsewhere in the archipelago and does not extend to this one. Travel through Maluku therefore adds no sub-national legal layer to the national position.
localsOnly: No Maluku-specific regulation, enforcement practice, service or protection body bearing on transgender residents was identified in the sources reviewed. Residents fall under the same national framework as the rest of Indonesia, and no local provision alters it.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Maluku is among the provinces reached by the national civil-registry outreach that issues electronic identity cards to transgender residents is not stated in the sources and remains unresolved.

Maluku-level police statistics, prosecution records and incident reports were not sourced, so the province's enforcement intensity cannot be compared with the national pattern; any provincial or district bylaw touching morality, dress or public conduct is likewise unresolved.
